what_happened.line: The Select Board found a violation of a Class 2 auto dealer license at 40 Summer Street and revoked the license effective immediately; the vote tallies were not audible.
The board allowed the sewer commission to retain special counsel for the Highfield village allocation agreement, to be paid from sewer funds.
The board chose to survey the community on an extra-large trash bag and thicker bags, and to revisit pay-as-you-throw with pricing on August 22.
The board discussed the T-Mobile Town Hall lease, a revenue source, with a ten-year bid or a Town Meeting vote for a longer term as options.
Earth removal permits were put on the August 22 agenda, with letters to permit holders about possible closure plans for idle sites.

why_it_matters: Pay-as-you-throw bag prices and sizes affect what households pay to throw out trash, and the multi-year contract terms, including a per-bag charge that rises with CPI, would bind the town beyond this year.
The T-Mobile lease brings in town revenue, and a longer term would likely need a Town Meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on it this fall.
The sewer counsel is paid from sewer funds rather than the general town budget, so it bears on sewer users' costs and not on the tax bill.
watch_next: August 22 Select Board meeting: pay-as-you-throw bag pricing, earth removal permits and the Town Hall paint color are all scheduled to return.
A possible fall Town Meeting vote on the T-Mobile Town Hall lease term.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the three Class II license and sewer counsel votes and on most figures and decisions, with several caption errors in names and warrant figures. The main difference is the bag price: our minutes give $4 per bag and a $3,775 order, while the official minutes give $20 per roll and a $3,775 investment, and ours records no vote outcomes.
